title: Air Force Tech Report: Rescue Tech
description:
Whether you’re climbing high in the mountains of Colorado, or flying over the Mississippi River tallgrass prairie, the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center, or AFRCC is always standing by to make sure your trip is a safe one. And what better way to stay safe than being prepared for emergencies with a beacon that transmits your location straight to the center responsible for sending help? After verifying a distress call, it only takes the click of a button, and Guard, Reserve, or active duty Airmen, the Civil Air Patrol, or local authorities will be on their way to save the day. Take a look at the process behind the  tech.

transcript.text: (Airplane engines thunder as it takes off)
- Flying,
hiking,
boating,
pass times many Americans enjoy.
But when things go wrong, they can go very wrong.
And when they do, the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center
or AFRCC, along with their Reserve Guard and DOD partners
are standing by to save the day.
- We are part of a network across the U.S. and around the
world that supports anybody who's in distress so, for us,
that's who which the DOD assets, Guard, Reserve, Active
Duty, could be Customs Border Patrol, depending who's the
closest and most capable asset.
- Using state of the art technology, like 400 megahurtz
speak-ins, the kind that you can pick up at any outdoor or
sporting goods store, and a series of low Earth orbit
satellites, the AFRCC is able to pinpoint distress signals
and send the help necessary to conduct rescue missions.
They also use radar and cellphone forensics, analyzing
data to quickly and accurately narrow in on where to search.
The process is a joint effort between Active Duty Air Force,
and other services like the Civil Air Patrol, The Guard and
Reserve, whoever has the capability necessary for a
particular mission. It's a well orchestrated process
that saves hundreds of lives each year.
(Indistinct radio conversation)
